name: Aab Gosht
subtitle: mutton chops poached in fennel-scented milk, pale and delicate

ingredients.note: aab gosht means water-meat, but milk is what carries it

ingredients.qty: 1 tbsp, tied in a square of muslin

ingredients.note: keeps the gravy pale where black pepper would speck it

prepNotes: Tie the fennel seeds in muslin so they can be fished out later; loose seeds in the finished gravy are unpleasant to eat.
Bring the milk to room temperature. Cold milk poured into a hot pan is the fastest way to make it catch.
Trim heavy fat off the chops — this dish should be delicate, and rendered fat makes the milk greasy.

steps.text: Bring the chops, water, garlic, bay leaf, both cardamoms, cloves, cinnamon, the muslin bag of fennel seeds and 1 tsp salt to a boil, then skim off the foam.
Simmer covered 45 minutes, until the meat is tender and pulling from the bone, then uncover and boil the liquid down to about 150ml.
steps.tip: Reducing the stock first concentrates the flavour; skip it and the milk simply dilutes everything.

steps.text: Remove the muslin bag and squeeze it out into the pan.
Add the milk in three additions, letting each come back to a bare simmer before the next goes in.
steps.tip: Three additions, and never a rolling boil. Milk added all at once and boiled hard will curdle around the meat.

steps.text: Stir in the fennel powder, dry ginger and white pepper.
Simmer uncovered on low for 25 minutes, stirring the base every few minutes with a flat spoon, until the gravy thinly coats the back of it.
steps.tip: Use a flat-ended spoon and scrape the base each time — milk scorches there long before you can smell it.

steps.text: Heat the ghee separately until it is nut-brown and pour it over the pan, giving it one stir.
Check the salt, rest 10 minutes off the heat and serve with plain rice or with a girda.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat on the lowest flame, stirring, and add a splash of milk to loosen; it will split if it boils.
